endorsements.quote: The specific tools (including model or platform name, version, and provider) and the purpose and scope of their use should be described in the Methods section and/or in the figure legends, in accordance with journal guidelines.

However, when such drafts are converted into editable formats (including vector graphics), systematically reviewed by qualified experts, and substantially revised or reconstructed to correct inaccuracies and adapt the content to the scientific question, they can serve as valuable starting points for producing publication-quality illustrations.

In this workflow, generative AI is used only as a tool for producing preliminary drafts and style suggestions, while clinicians and medical illustrators retain full control over the scientific content, anatomical accuracy, and final appearance of all figures ( Fig. 1 ) [ 3 , 8 , 9 , 14 ].
Provenance information should be preserved wherever technically feasible, and never deliberately removed to obscure the contribution of AI [ 11 ].
Therefore, a qualified clinician should carefully review and correct any AI-generated figure to avoid distorting clinically important structures [ 2 ].

unlisted_practices: Do not list AI tools as authors; human authors remain fully accountable for AI-assisted content in manuscripts.
Provide editors, upon request, with underlying source materials such as prompts, sketches, and intermediate drafts used to generate or modify AI-assisted figures.
Do not use AI-generated content in scientific figures solely for cosmetic or promotional purposes.
Clearly label AI-generated graphics used in non-scientific contexts such as journal covers and graphical abstracts.
Do not use AI to fabricate data or manipulate images in ways that misrepresent actual findings.
Avoid or use cautiously online image conversion services when identifiable or sensitive clinical information may be included.
Avoid direct use of realistic AI-generated portraits of pediatric patients; produce non-identifiable schematic illustrations that respect patient dignity.
Review journal AI policies at the time of manuscript submission because they evolve rapidly.
Do not upload confidential manuscripts or peer-review materials into generative AI tools.

screen.reason: This is a review and perspective/framework paper proposing workflows, ethical safeguards, and journal policy considerations for using generative AI to create medical illustrations in pediatric neurosurgery.
